newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Plavsic rejects november local elections.
newsitem.headline: Plavsic rejects november local elections.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic raised the stakes in her standoff with the international community on Friday by declaring there would be no municipal elections in the Bosnian Serb Republic in November.

"There will be no negotiations on November local elections in (Bosnian Serb republic), because we have finally said "no' to Frowick too", the Belgrade news agency Beta quoted Plavsic as saying to Serbian Radio Jagodina.
She was referring to Robert Frowick, U.S. head of the Bosnia mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which is charged with organising Bosnia's postwar elections.

Municipal elections were due to have been held last September 14, along with presidential, national and regional polls, but were postponed until late November because of irregularities in registering refugees.

Bosnian Serb leaders have toughened their opposition to local elections, fearing they could be voted out of power by Moslem refugees in their home towns where they were once a majority before being driven out.
Under the Dayton accord which ended the war last December, these refugees have the right to return to their homes to vote.
The Serbs have also baulked at joining Bosnia's joint governing bodies which were elected in September, effectively blocking the peace process laid down in Dayton, diplomats say.
The OSCE has been in intense negotiations with Plavsic to overcome her objections to the local polls being held under OSCE supervision, citing security problems.
"In an atmosphere of Moslem war threats and their terrorist actions...there are no conditions for holding local elections in November," Plavsic said.

Moslems have recently moved back into three villages within Serb territory in eastern Bosnia, raising tensions in the area. Three Moslems were arrested but later released after Serb police found illagel weapons oin one home.
The Serbs allege the men are not original inhabitants but military men preparing the villages as bridgeheads for possible future fighting.
Plavsic also noted the incident in nearby Lopari few days ago when a bus was fired upon and three people were wounded.
"I informed Frowick a few days ago that under such conditions of terrorism along our border we cannot accept local elections," she said.
